ORAL ORDER 1. Heard Mr.M.L.Rangras for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms.Vrunda Shah and learned advocate Mr.Lalit Patel appearing for the respondent no.2.
2. Matter is taken up finally with consent of the parties.

Hence, Rule.
3.
Learned A.P.P. Ms.Vrunda Shah and learned advocate Mr.Lalit Patel waive service of Rule for the respondent nos. 1 and 2 respectively.

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13920/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined 4.
Learned advocate Mr.M.L.Rangras, upon instructions, states that out of two draft amendments filed by the petitioner, this Court may grant the draft amendment dtd. 18th September, 2024.
Accordingly, the draft amendment dated 18th September, 2024 is granted.
To be carried out forthwith.

5. By way of this petition, the petitioner has prayed for quashing and setting aside the F.I.R. bearing C.R.No.I-2 of 2003 registered with CID Crime, Gandhinagar as well as the consequential proceedings being Criminal Case No.1045 of 2004 pending before the learned Chief Metropolitan Court, Ghee-Kanta, Ahmedabad under Sections 406, 420, 421, 422, 423, 424, 467, 468, 471, 120(B)
of the Indian Penal Code.

6. At the outset, it was submitted by learned advocate Mr.M.L.Rangras that all the dues of the bank is already paid and no due certificate is also produced on record and he points out to the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13920/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined affidavit filed by Mr.Ashutosh Kumar, who is authorized officer of the Punjab National Bank, whereby he has stated that there are no dues outstanding of the bank, however the bank cannot give consent for quashing of the F.I.R. as once the F.I.R. is registered, it is the State which becomes the complainant.

However,
the learned advocate Mr.Lalit Patel appearing for the bank confirms that there are no dues of the bank.
Learned advocate Mr.M.L.Rangras points out the series of orders,

whereby other persons,
who also availed the loan facility from the bank and against whom the F.I.R. is registered and upon payment of dues, the proceedings pursuant to the registration of the F.I.R., were quashed by the coordinate bench of this Court and therefore, learned advocate Mr.M.L.Rangras states that in view of the fact that the present petitioner also has repaid the loan amount and no due certificate is also issued in favour of the present petitioner as well the petitioner's case also be NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13920/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined considered in similar manner and all the proceedings qua present petitioner pursuant to the F.I.R. in question are required to be quashed.
7. I have heard learned advocates for the respective parties.
8.

In view of the affidavit of the bank produced on record and in view of the submissions made by the parties and also considering the fact that the amount has already been paid and no due certificate has been produced, the case of the present applicant deserves to be considered.
Moreover,

considering the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court including the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a judgment in case of Madan Mohan Abbot V/s State of Punjab reported in (2008) 4 SCC 582, as well as in a judgment in case Shiji @ Pappu & Ors. Vs.Radhika & Anr.,
reported in AIR 2012 SC 499, wherein it has been observed that if the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/13920/2024 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined continuation of the proceedings would be an empty formality then the exercise of discretion under Section 482 of the criminal Procedure Code would be justified, the present application deserves to be allowed.

sentences.text: Therefore, the present petition stands allowed in terms of Para No.8(B).

The F.I.R. bearing C.R.No.I-2 of 2003 registered with CID Crime, Gandhinagar as well as the consequential proceedings being Criminal Case No.1045 of 2004 pending before the learned Chief Metropolitan Court, Ghee-Kanta, Ahmedabad is hereby quashed and set aside.
